sections.name: summary
sections.value: pij ships pod templates and type definitions as versioned originals. A pod command names a template by path or as `shipped:<name>[@v<n>]`; `adopt` and `init` copy them to governance or `--into <path>`; `template-diff` shows upstream changes and applies nothing. Nothing launches a seat.

sections.name: goals
value: A repo owns its templates wherever it keeps them, and pij's shipped set improves for everyone.

value.claim: Shipped originals under `templates/pods/<name>/v<N>/`, embedded like role templates, never edited after they ship (a pinned hash per version).

`pij pod adopt <name> [--into <path>] --why <text>` copies a shipped template to governance (default) or the path, recording its version, in one writer commit. Every pod command says which template it read: a path, or a shipped name and version.
`pij pod template-diff <path>` shows what changed upstream since the copy's version and applies nothing.

`pij community init --seeds all --templates <names> [--into <path>] --why <text>` copies the ten type definitions into governance and the named templates into governance or the path, one commit per place, and prints what it wrote and where.
Cost: adopt, init and export are one writer commit each (init one per place); diff and listing are in-process. No seat launched; no loop, poll or timer.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Role template catalog (crates/daemon/src/community/templates.rs): SHIPPED, the pinned hashes and template-diff are the model.

value.risk: A copy at a path in the main repo is edited by hand.
value.mitigation: That is its purpose: the repo owns its copy; diff still compares it with upstream.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Cost: one writer commit per adopt, init place or export; reads in-process; no seat launched; no loop, poll or timer.
No permission rule changes (PRD 003); no daemon enforcement of a type's rules; no existing JSON field removed or renamed.
Builds nice-19 through `just shared-build`, one at a time.
